Taco Bell Grilled Cheese Steak Burrito at Home!  I'm a former Taco Bell employee, and this is one of my favorite menu items! 🥩 STEAK 1 lb top sirloin, thinly sliced ½ tsp salt 1 tsp brown sugar ½ tsp beef bouillon ⅛ tsp cocoa powder ½ tsp onion powder ½ tsp garlic powder ¼ tsp paprika ½ tsp cornstarch Sauce: ½ cup water 1 tsp beef bouillon 1 tsp brown sugar ½ tsp onion powder ½ tsp garlic powder ⅛ tsp cocoa powder ½ tsp cornstarch Cut steak against the grain for tenderness. Toss with dry seasonings and sear in a little oil over medium-high heat. Whisk sauce ingredients together, pour over steak and simmer gently until cooked through and lightly thickened. Add water if needed. 🍚 SEASONED RICE 2 cups white rice 2 cups water 2 tbsp Knorr Tomato Chicken Bouillon 2 tbsp oil ¾ tsp garlic powder ½ tsp onion powder ½ tsp paprika Rinse rice until water runs mostly clear. Add everything to rice cooker, stir and use the white rice setting. Fluff before serving. Adjust water to your cooker's instructions. 🌶️ CHIPOTLE SAUCE 1 cup mayonnaise 1–2 chipotle peppers in adobo 1 tsp adobo sauce ½ tsp each chili powder, sugar, salt ¼ tsp each garlic powder, onion powder, paprika Blend until creamy. Refrigerate until needed.   🌯 ASSEMBLY Large flour tortillas Seasoned steak and rice Nacho cheese (I use frito's jalapeno cheddar) Chipotle sauce Tortilla strips Sour cream Shredded Mexican-blend cheese Warm tortilla so it's flexible. Layer rice, steak, nacho cheese, chipotle sauce, tortilla strips and sour cream. Fold sides in and roll tightly. Toast seam-side down in a skillet. Remove, sprinkle cheese into a nonstick skillet and place burrito on top, untoasted side down. Cook over medium-low until cheese melts and turns golden. Let cool slightly so the cheese sets on the tortilla. Is this easier than just spending $8 at Taco Bell? Absolutely not. 😂 But we order these often enough that I love knowing how to make them at home! Want a separate tutorial for the steak, rice or sauce? Tell me which one! #tacobellathome #grilledcheeseburrito #tacobellrecipes #tacobellcopycat #homemadefastfood

Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
I'm a former Taco Bell employee and I'm showing you how to recreate your favorite Taco Bell menu items at home and today we're making my personal favorite, the steak grilled cheese burrito. And dare I say, this one turned out better than Taco Bell. Now there are quite a few layers to this one, so let's just jump right in. First is the creamy chipotle sauce. We're starting with a mayonnaise base, adding some chipotle peppers in adobo, a few seasonings, and blending everything together until it's nice and creamy. I'll include all of the exact measurements in the caption, but I'll also put some easier substitutions in the corner of the video. They might not be quite as accurate, but if you're just looking for a quick and easy alternative, I've tried them, they'll get the job done. Next is the rice, which is actually really simple. I'm using regular long grain white rice, rinsing it until the water runs mostly clear, then adding some of this tomato and chicken bouillon powder, a little oil, and a handful of seasonings, and everything goes straight into the rice cooker on the white rice setting. Now the steak is probably one of the hardest Taco Bell ingredients to recreate at home. Their steak is incredibly flavorful and has this really soft, tender texture that's difficult to recreate with regular steak. And considering how expensive steak is, I think it's safe to assume that Taco Bell isn't exactly throwing premium cuts of beef into our $8 burritos. So I'm using top sirloin, which is a relatively affordable option, cutting it in the strips about 2 inches wide before slicing those into thin, fajita-sized pieces, and you want to make sure you're cutting against the grain for the most tender result. Now I actually looked up Taco Bell's published ingredient list, and one thing I found interesting is that their steak uses both a seasoning and a sauce with a lot of the same ingredients in both. So we're going to season our steak, give it a quick sear in a hot skillet, then finish cooking it in a savory sauce that reinforces all of those same flavors, which also helps keep the steak nice and juicy and tender rather than drying it out. And with all of our components ready, we can finally assemble this thing. Start with a warm burrito-sized flour tortilla, add on a scoop of our seasoned rice, some of that steak, a drizzle of warm nacho cheese, homemade chipotle sauce, some crunchy tortilla strips, and finally a little sour cream. Wrap everything up nice and tight, and we've got a perfectly good burrito, but we didn't come all this way to make a regular burrito. We need to make it a grilled cheese burrito. Taco Bell uses a clamshell grill to get that crispy, cheesy exterior, which I'm assuming most of us don't have sitting on our kitchen counter, so instead we're going to heat a skillet, place our burrito seamside down, and toast that first to help seal everything together. Then remove the burrito, add a sheet of parchment paper to our skillet, sprinkle on some shredded Mexican blend cheese, and place the burrito back on top, this time with the untoasted side facing down. Let that cook until the cheese is melted and starting to get those nice golden edges, then carefully lift the burrito out with the parchment paper still attached, wrap it up, and let it cool just slightly. This gives the cheese a chance to set and really stick to the outside of your burrito. And there you have it, a homemade steak grilled cheese burrito. Now I'm not going to pretend this is a quick and easy dinner. There are a lot of steps, and for some of you it's probably worth paying the $8 and just letting Taco Bell do the work, but these are genuinely our favorite things to order, and we probably get them a few times a month, so for me it's worth at least knowing how to make them at home. And if you want a more detailed version of any of the individual components, whether that's the rice, the chipotle sauce, or the steak, let me know in the comments and I can share those recipes separately.
